analyst.summary: Hyundai Motor India's FY26 was a year of quiet deceleration: domestic volumes fell 2.3% and the company slipped from India's No.2 auto brand to No.4 as Mahindra and Tata's SUV-led pushes out-competed it, while full-year profit was flat-to-down (Rs.5,432 cr vs Rs.5,640 cr) with a sharp Q4 margin squeeze (EBITDA margin 10.4% vs 14.1% a year earlier). April and May 2026 opened FY27 on a genuinely stronger footing before a one-off supplier-fire disruption dented June's domestic numbers; management is responding with its highest-ever capex (Rs.7,500 crore), two new SUV launches, and continued ramp-up of the new Talegaon plant. Two structural watch-items temper the recovery case: the royalty paid to the Korean parent was permanently raised to 3.5% of revenue (from ~2.25-2.5%), a fixed drag on minority shareholders' economics, and Hyundai's electric-vehicle push (the Creta Electric) is running well below its own 15% EV-mix target at under 4% share. At roughly 29x trailing earnings -- in line with Maruti despite Maruti holding the market's top rank -- the stock is not pricing in either the competitive setback or these structural drags, so we rate it Hold: a name to monitor through the FY27 launch cycle rather than add to.
